:::{#thm-moore-penrose-least-squares}
#### The Moore-Penrose inverse gives a least squares solution

Let $\matr{A}$ be $m \times n$ and $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$.
Then $\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$ is a least squares solution (@def-least-squares) of $\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$.
Moreover, a vector $\vecf{x} \in \reals^n$ is a least squares solution [if and only if](proof-writing.qmd#def-iff)

$$
\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \matr{A}\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}.
$$

:::

::: proof

Let $\matr{P} = \matr{A}\matr{A}^+$.
By conditions 3 and 1 of @def-moore-penrose, $\tp{\matr{P}} = \matr{P}$ and $\matr{P}\matr{A} = \matr{A}$.
Hence

$$
\ba
\tp{\matr{A}}(\matr{I} - \matr{P})
&= \tp{\matr{A}} - \tp{\matr{A}}\matr{P}
&& \text{(distributing)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}} - \tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{\matr{P}}
&& (\tp{\matr{P}} = \matr{P})
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}} - \tp{(\matr{P}\matr{A})}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}} - \tp{\matr{A}}
&& (\matr{P}\matr{A} = \matr{A})
\\
&= \matr{0}.
\ea
$$

For every $\vecf{x} \in \reals^n$, write $\vecf{b} - \matr{A}\vecf{x} = \vecf{u} + \vecf{v}$ with

$$
\vecf{u} = \vecf{b} - \matr{P}\vecf{b}
\qquad \text{and} \qquad
\vecf{v} = \matr{P}\vecf{b} - \matr{A}\vecf{x} = \matr{A}(\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} - \vecf{x}).
$$

Their [inner product](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-inner-product) is

$$
\ba
\dprod{\vecf{v}}{\vecf{u}}
&= \tp{(\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} - \vecf{x})}\,\tp{\matr{A}}(\matr{I} - \matr{P})\vecf{b}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= 0,
&& (\tp{\matr{A}}(\matr{I} - \matr{P}) = \matr{0})
\ea
$$

so $\norm{\vecf{b} - \matr{A}\vecf{x}}^2 = \norm{\vecf{u}}^2 + \norm{\vecf{v}}^2$.
That is,

$$
\norm{\vecf{b} - \matr{A}\vecf{x}}^2
= \norm{\vecf{b} - \matr{P}\vecf{b}}^2 + \norm{\matr{A}(\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} - \vecf{x})}^2.
$$

The first summand does not involve $\vecf{x}$,
and the second is nonnegative,
with a zero at $\vecf{x} = \matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$.
So $\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$ minimizes $\norm{\vecf{b} - \matr{A}\vecf{x}}$,
and the smallest [norm](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-norm) is $\norm{\vecf{b} - \matr{P}\vecf{b}}$.
A vector $\vecf{x}$ attains that norm [if and only if](proof-writing.qmd#def-iff) $\matr{A}(\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} - \vecf{x}) = \vecf{0}$,
which is $\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \matr{A}\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$.

:::
